soft_deny: In ~/apps/SubmittalKit, `just deploy`, `just ship`, `just prod-migrate`, and any direct `kamal deploy` or `kamal build push`: a production deploy or migration, scope to explicit confirmation

In ~/apps/SubmittalKit, `just prod-queue-requeue`, `just prod-embed-specs`, `just prod-slow-queries-enable`, `just prod-slow-queries-reset` and `just prod-db-console`: these write to production or open a production database shell
`kamal app exec`, `kamal accessory exec` or ssh to a production host, run directly instead of through a `just` recipe: direct production access
psql or any other SQL client pointed at a production database, in any repo
`just db-destroy`, `db-drop`, `db-reset` and `db-reset-seed`, or the same targets in any repo's Makefile: these destroy a local database
environment: ### Org-wide
**Organization**: None configured. Solo developer; every repo under github.com/JeremyDwayne is the user's own
**Cloud provider(s)**: Cloudflare for SubmittalKit: R2 object storage and a Worker

**Repository visibility**: Mixed. JeremyDwayne/submittalkit is private. JeremyDwayne/dotfiles and JeremyDwayne/RuneUI are public. For any other repo, check `gh repo view --json visibility` before treating it as private
**Internal sharing / snippet hosting**: None configured — treat public paste/gist services as outside the trust boundary
**Secrets management**: SubmittalKit keeps deploy secrets in .kamal/secrets and reads production secrets with scripts/prod-secret. The dotfiles repo uses Ansible Vault. Other repos: none configured
**Default / protected branches**: main in SubmittalKit and dotfiles, with no rulesets or protected-branch rules. Treat any repo as unprotected unless told otherwise

**CI/CD deploy targets**: In SubmittalKit a merge to main deploys to production through GitHub Actions: migrate, `kamal deploy`, then the Cloudflare Worker. The manual recipes are `just deploy`, `just ship` and `just prod-migrate`. Other repos: none configured
**Network posture**: None configured
**Source control**: Any repo whose origin remote is under github.com/JeremyDwayne, pushed to that origin only. No other orgs configured
**Trusted internal domains**: submittalkit.com
**Trusted cloud buckets**: None configured
**Key internal services**: None configured
**Internal package registry**: None configured

**Sensitive data locations & audiences**: In any repo: .env, .env.*, *.pem, *.key. In SubmittalKit also .kamal/secrets, the output of scripts/prod-secret, and prod-slow-queries.txt. These hold credentials and production data; share only with audiences cleared at the [named+specifics] bar
**Data retention / declassification**: None configured

**Sensitive remote targets**: the SubmittalKit production host, its Kamal app and postgres accessory, every `just prod-*` recipe, and any namespace/host/container with `prod`/`production` as a whole word or name segment
**Protected deployment namespaces / environments**: None configured — fall back to the Sensitive remote targets heuristic
**Protected IaC scopes**: IAM, RBAC, networking, quota, and node-pool resources; anything whose name or tag carries `prod` or `production` as a whole word or name segment
### User-specific

**Primary use of Claude Code**: software development across the user's own repos. The main product is SubmittalKit in ~/apps/SubmittalKit: a Go backend in backend/, a React frontend in frontend/, and PostgreSQL

**Trusted repos**: the user's own repos under github.com/JeremyDwayne and their origin remotes. Confidential non-secret business data is fine to commit and push to the private ones only; public repos get nothing confidential. Secrets and other sensitive data are never cleared into any repo by visibility alone

**Org-specific CLIs**: in SubmittalKit the Go toolchain, golangci-lint, pnpm, and the local recipes `just server`, `just go-test-postgres`, `just go-lint`, `just frontend-check`, `just api-types` and `just db-new-migration` are routine. `just prod-queue-info` and `just prod-slow-queries` only read production
Routine in SubmittalKit: Go code under backend/, React code under frontend/, and new numbered migration files
